natural_body: 40% discounts raise acquisition and revenue but hurt retention and renewals.

first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both down this quarter, and prior durable memories (31, 86, 91) show that simplifying onboarding and in-product activation messaging reliably improved these exact metrics without noted retention harm. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is already flagged as raising acquisition but damaging retention and renewals, which conflicts with the objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, especially against a competitor racing to the bottom on price—so it's deprioritized despite competitive pressure. With only one experiment slot, I want to verify the archived records for memory_86 (onboarding) and memory_91 (activation messaging) since they are the two most directly relevant to the current declines and could point to different interventions; confirming their original experimental conditions will clarify which lever is more likely to reverse this quarter's drop. Referral incentives (memory_57) and enterprise sales-assist (memory_44) are promising but address different funnel stages and don't directly target the onboarding/activation declines observed now. Tentatively leaning toward simplify_onboarding as it has two corroborating memories (31 and 86) and directly targets the metric that dropped (onboarding completion), which likely drives the activation decline downstream.
